newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge clears Foxmeyer chapter 7 liquidation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge clears Foxmeyer chapter 7 liquidation.

text.p: Foxmeyer Drug Co and five affiliates received approval at 5 p.m. Tuesday to convert their chapter 11 reorganization bankrutpcy cases to chapter 7 liquidation, an attorney said.

According to an attorney for the unsecured creditors' committee, Francis Monaco, Judge Helen Balick of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware approved Foxmeyer's motion for the conversion at a hearing Tuesday. Monaco told Reuters the committee is dissolved as a result of the conversion and will be replaced by a liquidating trustee.

The FoxMeyer entities, affiliates of Avatex Corp, said in court papers filed Tuesday that the purpose of the conversion was to "obtain a consensual plan of liquidation pursuant to which their assets...could be fairly distributed among their remaining liabilities."

Foxmeyer said monthly administration costs as high as $2 million and a pending lawsuit were among the factors for converting to chapter 7 because a liquidation trustee would be "a central source of control" for reducing costs and managing litigation.
"The debtors believe a conversion will serve the best interests of their estates, creditors and stockholders and will not prejudice the rights of any party in these cases," court papers say.

Foxmeyer was one of the largest wholesale drug distribution companies in the U.S. before its bankruptcy filing on August 27, 1996. It sold substantially all business operations and related assets to McKesson Corp on November 8, 1996 after being "forced (to) by mounting business problems and rapidly escalating financial losses," court papers say.
The affiliates include Foxmeyer Corp, HealthCare Transportation system Inc, Merchandise Coordinator Services Corp, FoxMeyer Software Inc, and HealthMart Inc.
